interpretations: Use the average of all nonmissing `Laboratory.HGB` values as the overall average. Return patients whose own average is above it, with their ID, own average, difference from the overall average, and difference from the mean of the qualifying patients’ averages; sort by the last difference descending and take 10.

Use the mean of each patient’s nonmissing `HGB` average as the overall average, giving each patient equal weight. Return the same four values for qualifying patients; sort by the last difference descending and take 10.
queries:
WITH overall AS (
    SELECT AVG(HGB) AS avg_hgb
    FROM Laboratory
),
patient_averages AS (
    SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) AS avg_hgb
    FROM Laboratory
    GROUP BY ID
),
qualifying AS (
    SELECT p.ID, p.avg_hgb
    FROM patient_averages AS p
    CROSS JOIN overall AS o
    WHERE p.avg_hgb > o.avg_hgb
)
SELECT
    q.ID,
    q.avg_hgb AS patient_average,
    q.avg_hgb - o.avg_hgb AS difference_from_overall,
    q.avg_hgb - (SELECT AVG(avg_hgb) FROM qualifying) AS difference_from_qualifying_mean
FROM qualifying AS q
CROSS JOIN overall AS o
ORDER BY difference_from_qualifying_mean DESC
LIMIT 10

WITH patient_averages AS (
    SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) AS patient_avg_hgb
    FROM Laboratory
    WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY ID
),
overall_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(patient_avg_hgb) AS overall_avg_hgb
    FROM patient_averages
)
SELECT
    p.ID,
    p.patient_avg_hgb,
    o.overall_avg_hgb,
    p.patient_avg_hgb - o.overall_avg_hgb AS difference
FROM patient_averages AS p
CROSS JOIN overall_average AS o
WHERE p.patient_avg_hgb > o.overall_avg_hgb
ORDER BY difference DESC
LIMIT 10
